chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Thamon Hayes's band and Jesse Stone's Idaho
summary: Thamon Hayes's band had good arrangements by Jesse Stone, who wrote Idaho.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: be working you know. Tough times were kind of slim in those days. But we had a great band at that time. Thamon Hayes's band.
He was a trombone player also.

Yeah. Yeah. We had a good arrangement -- good arrangements of Jesse Stone. He really could make some arrangements. You know, he's the one that wrote "Idaho." That's his number, and I think he's got several other numbers. But that "Idaho" is one that became very famous. All the guys used to play that. All the modern guys used to play that.
That's funny -- that's so nice too, nobody plays it anymore.
Yeah, Byrd and all them used to play that -- that was one of their numbers.
